premises.text: Many Americans have subprime credit and are afraid to check their score
premises.evidence_span: One out of two Americans has subprime credit. And six out of ten adults have not checked their score in the last year. One out of three has never checked their score. And you want to know why? It's because they are afraid.

premises.text: Credit reports often contain errors that are costly
premises.evidence_span: Eight out of ten credit reports have an error. And that's expensive.

premises.text: Improving credit scores is essential for financial opportunities
premises.evidence_span: the cost of good credit versus bad credit is over $5,000 annually. It can keep you from the home or job of your choice.

premises.text: A structured process can help users improve their credit scores
premises.evidence_span: we take you through a set of credit-improving tactics based on our decision tree.

premises.text: Behavioral economics can drive credit score improvement
premises.evidence_span: we continue with behavioral economics to create a concrete set of actions to help you improve your credit score.

premises.text: Unique data from users can create financial segments and personas
premises.evidence_span: we're giving psychographic, behavioral, and historical credit data that we can then leverage to create financial user segments and personas.

premises.text: The market for financial services is large and underserved
premises.evidence_span: There are 100 million Americans looking to access $150 billion in financial services.

value.text: Americans can take control of their financial lives and improve their credit scores
value.evidence_span: we're on a mission to help everyday Americans take control of their financial lives.

notes: Traction metrics and specific user counts excluded as they do not support premises.
